summary: Clean a newly created NFS or SMB3 mount unit after failed first start so fresh registration can safely retry the same ID. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: The operator still corrects the remote service and submits a fresh registration request; no guide step or supported destination changes.

api.reason: No route or schema changes. Failed first NFS/SMB3 mount preparation removes a newly created Core unit, permitting a new same-ID request after service recovery; an uncertain rollback remains a failure.

roadmap.reason: Fixes safe registration retry already required by the destination plan.

state.reason: No new durable record is introduced; this removes a failed local managed mount unit before any repository is committed.

verification.method: A disposable SMB3 first registration failed before the new share was active and left a Core unit; fresh same-ID requests failed after share recovery. A focused regression for failed first start and a concurrent preparation regression failed before their respective corrections and passed afterward under focused race checking. The full vmhost package passed. Independent review found the overlap hazard, then re-reviewed serialization and cleanup with no further concrete finding. A fresh current-source disposable Core failed first registration against a new absent share without leaving a unit/mount/repo, retained the exact failed replay, then accepted a fresh credential/request for the same repository ID after the share became available. Core access passed; the failed handoff was already retired and the active one ready. Existing point and source hashes stayed unchanged. All fixture processes stopped.
verification.limits: The retained old orphan is a fixture artifact from the pre-fix binary. Broader mount failures and forge CI remain open.
